summary: Omsk Oblast is a federal subject of the Russian Federation and stands under the national legal framework, which prohibits legal gender recognition, bans transition-related healthcare and treats the designated "international LGBT movement" as extremist. The sources reviewed for this record contain no oblast-level statute, court ruling, police action, incident or institutional practice bearing on transgender visitors or residents. The national assessment applies in full.
tangentialFactors: No oblast-specific adjacent factor was identified. The UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression for Russia (version 2.0, June 2025) and the Human Rights Watch reporting of 30 June 2025 used for this record are national in scope and carry no Omsk Oblast detail.
localsOnly: No resident-facing fact specific to Omsk Oblast was located. Transgender residents of the oblast are governed by the same national rules on legal gender recognition, transition-related healthcare and extremist-symbol enforcement as the rest of the federation, and no oblast-level protection, service or enforcement practice is documented in the sources reviewed.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved: whether Omsk Oblast courts, police or prosecutors apply the national statutes at a rate or severity different from the national baseline. No oblast-level case counts, conviction figures or local administrative data were located, and the national figures cannot be disaggregated to this federal subject from the sources available.
